<description>
Enable `optin.performance.Padding` with the default of 24 bytes (made explicit in the clang-tidy config), after fixing warnings for more padding than that. Enabling it at this point would be to catch regressions above this amount.

Based on #36501, which reorders `CBlockIndex` to save 8 bytes (`clang-tidy` also warns about this). Wondering if contributors/reviewers think this is worthwhile given we may make that refactor? Also not sure if it's possible for us to enable this generally, as padding will differ depending on various factors.
</description>

<commits>
c2dedba48f Reorder CBlockIndex members to save 8 bytes

On a windows x64 build, CBlockIndex size is 160 bytes. Moving one field
somewhere else makes the class lose less bytes due to padding to respect
the 8-byte alignment

For a ~1M block height, this saves about 8M of Ram without doing
anything else.

e90a267db7 Reorder CNode and CConnman members to reduce padding

db7b3535c5 Reorder CTxMemPool members to reduce padding

f6879ec26a wallet: reorder CWalletTx members to reduce padding

5d72e30b3a net_processing: reorder Peer members to reduce padding

0c4d15f589 rpc: reorder CRPCConvertParam members to reduce padding

c2f15bb647 clang-tidy: add clang-analyzer-optin.performance.Padding

In #36501 we reordered fields in `CBlock` to save 8 bytes.
Add the clang-tidy padding check, leave the warning threshold
(explicitly) at the default of 24 bytes.

https://clang.llvm.org/docs/analyzer/checkers.html#optin-performance-padding
</commits>
